description:
For twelve years Walter was the only dog in the house. Then Noodle arrived in a box with a bow, and suddenly nobody notices the leash, the slippers or his best bark at the mail carrier. Walter has a plan. So does everybody else.

lines.text: Twelve years. For twelve years, I was the only dog in this house.
Hi! I am Noodle! I live here now! Is that your bed? That is my bed now!
It arrived on Tuesday. In a box. With a bow on it.
I was the present! You were not the present. I checked.
Oh my goodness, look at his little ears! Look at his little everything!
I also have ears. I have had these ears since two thousand fourteen.
Walter, buddy, not now. Noodle is trying on his little sweater.
He has a sweater. I have a scarf from a yard sale. Nobody asked about the scarf.
Fine. Step one. The leash. Nobody ignores the leash.
What is a leash? Is it food? I think it is food.
I dropped it at her feet. Very gently. Like a gift.
Thank you, Walter. Noodle, who is a good boy? You are!
She stepped over the leash. She stepped over me. Then she stepped over the leash again.
So I brought her slipper. Then the other slipper. Then the entire laundry basket.
He carried the basket up the stairs! With his face! I clapped with my feet!
Who keeps putting socks on the stairs? Noodle, did you do that? So clever!
Clever. He has never carried anything in his life. He cannot carry a tune.
I can carry a tune! Bark bark, bark bark bark!
That is not a tune. That is a complaint.
Step two. The mail carrier. Twelve o'clock. My greatest performance.
Afternoon, folks. Got a big box here for Kim.
For twelve years I have barked at this man. For twelve years, he has been terrified.
Woof. Woof. Wooof. Ruff. That last one was in a deep voice.
Well hello, little guy! Look at that tiny sweater!
He walked right past me. To the puppy. With a biscuit.
Oh, hey Walter. Love the singing today. Very relaxing.
Singing. Twelve years of protecting this house, and he thinks I am a radio.
I got the biscuit! It tasted like the mailbox! I love the mailbox!
Step three. The big one. I lay down on the rug. Very still. Very dramatic.
Is he sleeping? Is he a rug now? Can I sit on him?
Do not sit on me. I am being tragic.
Noodle! Treat time! Come here, sweet boy!
She walked over me to give him a treat. I was tragic for eleven minutes. Nobody came.
I came! I came back for your treat too! I ate it! You are welcome!
Even the cat came over. She looked at me. She shook her head. She left.
We have a cat?
We have had a cat for nine years. She also pays me no mind.
Fine. You want to ignore Walter? Walter will ignore all of you.
I packed a bag. One sock, one tennis ball, and a picture of me as a puppy.
You were a puppy? You were cute! What happened?
Twelve years happened. I am moving to the porch. Forever. Or until dinner.
Walter? Walter, where are you going? Wait! Not yet!
Oh, now she notices. Now that I have a sock in a bag.
Kim! They are all here! Should I open the gate?
Open the gate? Who is here? Why is the mail man still here?
Surprise! Happy twelve years, Walter!
The whole yard was full of dogs. Every dog on the street. And a cake shaped like a slipper.
We had to keep you busy all week, buddy. Noodle was the distraction.
I was undercover! I do not even like sweaters. It itches in the armpits.
You ate my treat. Was that undercover too?
No. That was just me.
And I was undercover too. The box is your party hat.
So you were never relaxed by my singing.
Honestly? I have been scared of you for twelve years. Great job, Walter.
I knew it. Twelve years of hard work, finally paid off.
You are the best boy in this house. You always were.
I am the second best boy! I just found out! I am so happy about it!
So all week, you paid me no mind. On purpose.
Every single second. It was the hardest week of my life.
Walter? Now that we are friends, can I have your bed?
You can have half.
I already ate half.
Then I am sleeping in the sweater.
